Kenya transfers (FOF, "Empire" group). The USAO release on Sept 4, 2025 says Abdiaziz Farah (convicted, sentenced to 28 years) "sent millions of dollars in fraud proceeds abroad." Among other things, his brother in Kenya said he had received "$1,287,000" in the days before Dec 27, 2021. The release describes a $300,000 transfer labeled "family support," an apartment building in Nairobi, and land in Mandera, Kenya. The brother, Ahmednaji Sheikh, was charged with conspiracy to commit international money laundering (allegation): irs.gov
EIDBI. Abdinajib Yussuf allegedly "sent more than $200,000 in fraud proceeds to Kenya" (USAO, Dec 18, 2025, IRS-CI mirror above).

HSS. Asad Adow allegedly used proceeds "to invest in real estate in Kenya" (USAO, Sept 18, 2025). Pristine Health defendants allegedly spent proceeds on travel to London, Sydney, Dubai, Istanbul, and Saudi Arabia (USAO, Dec 18, 2025).
more: Treasury, official statements. On Jan 9, 2026, FinCEN issued four notices of investigation to Minnesota money services businesses, a Geographic Targeting Order (reports on transfers of $3,000 or more to beneficiaries outside the U.S. from banks and transmitters in Hennepin and Ramsey counties), and an alert on child-nutrition fraud. Treasury said law enforcement "has limited insight into the persons located abroad who receive the proceeds": home.treasury.gov; GTO: federalregister.gov. The GTO was renewed Aug 7, 2026, with Treasury saying "a portion of which has been laundered overseas." Neither release names Somalia or al-Shabaab: home.treasury.gov; federalregister.gov

No terrorism charges. No defendant in these fraud cases has been charged under 18 U.S.C. 2339B (material support to a designated FTO) or 18 U.S.C. 2339C (terrorism financing), based on every DOJ release reviewed.

entries.headline: White House digital director Rob Flaherty to Twitter, Feb 6, 2021

lines: “Cannot stress the degree to which this needs to be resolved immediately.”

About a parody account of President Biden's granddaughter; Twitter suspended it within about 45 minutes (district court ruling, p. 9). The Supreme Court later noted (fn. 4) that this impersonation request was mischaracterized as a censorship request.
W.D. La. ruling, ECF 293 Murthy v. Missouri
“Are you guys f***ing serious? I want an answer on what happened here and I want it today.”
Quoted in the district court's findings (p. 23). The profanity is shown with letters masked; the court record prints the word in full.
“We're flagging problematic posts for Facebook … there's about 12 people who are producing 65 percent of anti-vaccine misinformation.”

The next day: “we're in regular touch with social media platforms … You all make decisions, just like the social media platforms make decisions,” and “You shouldn't be banned from one platform and not others.”
Briefing transcript, Jul 15 Briefing transcript, Jul 16
“Impose clear consequences for accounts that repeatedly violate platform policies.”

It also urged platforms to “prioritize early detection of misinformation ‘super-spreaders’ and repeat offenders.” Its definition of misinformation covers a true anecdote that is “highly misleading,” and it warns against “conflating controversial or unorthodox claims with misinformation.”
Three days later: “Facebook isn't killing people; these 12 people who are out there giving misinformation—anyone listening to it is getting hurt by it. It's killing people.”
PBS raw video Official transcript, Jul 19

Also: “I believe the government pressure was wrong” and “Ultimately, it was our decision whether or not to take content down, and we own our decisions.” On the laptop story he describes a general FBI warning, not one naming the Post story, and says “in retrospect, we shouldn't have demoted the story.”

entries.headline: The short answer: no president, from either party, sets the price of gas. Oil is priced on a world market, and oil is about half…

lines: The short answer: no president, from either party, sets the price of gas. Oil is priced on a world market, and oil is about half of every gallon. A president can nudge supply a little (selling emergency reserve oil, sanctions, drilling leases, Jones Act waivers). That is a nudge, not a price.
record.label: Verified by SwampForce

entries.headline: Why only seven OPEC+ countries? OPEC press releases

lines: The monthly OPEC+ decisions are made by the countries that added extra voluntary cuts in 2023. That group had eight members; the United Arab Emirates left OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, 2026 (WAM, Apr 28, 2026), leaving seven. On Sep 6, 2026 the seven kept October the same as September. The 2023 cut of about 1.65 million barrels a day was brought back in steps; the Aug 2, 2026 step was 188,000 barrels a day for September. Next meeting: Oct 4, 2026.

entries.headline: Bottom line: About 79% of today's price is crude, taxes, a normal refining margin and station costs.

lines: About 12.5% is a war-shortage premium whose cause is documented but whose size nobody has measured. About 9% (40¢) is the unusually wide gap between world and U.S. crude prices. No primary record we found explains that gap, and it is the best lead for anyone asking where the extra money goes. The whole increase since 2008 sits in refining. Taxes are up 12¢, and the station slice is currently lower. After inflation, gas is still below the 2008 peak: $4.114 then equals about $6.27 today (BLS CPI-U).

entries.headline: 2. Wholesale gasoline did not follow crude down.

lines: From Jun 1 to Jul 6, 2026, WTI fell 54.7¢/gal and Brent 65.1¢. Gulf Coast wholesale gasoline fell only 11.0¢, while U.S. retail fell 52.8¢. The retail-minus-wholesale spread dropped from $1.157 to $0.739. The DOJ and FTC wrote on Jul 3 that too much of the crude decline was being "withheld" (DOJ/FTC letter). The EIA numbers put the hold-up at the wholesale/refining stage, not at stations. The letter is a statement of concern. No finding.

entries.headline: 4. Refiners paid out almost all their profit while capacity shrank.

lines: Valero, Marathon Petroleum and Phillips 66 reported $81.7B of net income for 2022–2025. In the same years they spent $61.5B on buybacks and $18.1B on dividends, which is 97% of net income (SEC 10-Ks: Valero, Marathon, Phillips 66). U.S. operable capacity fell from 18,976 to 18,027 thousand b/d between Jan 2020 and Jun 2026 (EIA). Five refiners (those three plus PBF and HF Sinclair) earned $17.3B in the first half of 2026 alone. These are legal choices. No regulator has found that capacity was withheld to raise prices.
record.label: Verified by SwampForce

entries.headline: 5. Speculators are unusually long gasoline, not crude.

lines: Managed-money funds held a net long of 92,848 RBOB gasoline contracts on Sep 8, 2026. That is 25.4% of open interest and the highest since April 2012, above the 2008 peak (62,535; 23.3%) and the 2022 peak (81,212; 24.8%). In crude they are modest: 111,731 contracts (5.8%), against 279,511 (15.2%) in 2022 (CFTC COT). Large positions are legal, and positioning is not manipulation. We found no 2026 CFTC manipulation case.
record.label: Verified by SwampForce

The low-carbon fuel standard adds about 18¢ and cap-and-invest about 23¢ (CEC FAQ). Los Angeles wholesale runs 23.5¢ above the Gulf Coast. That leaves about 48¢ unexplained by these records. California's market watchdog reports a 31¢ branded-vs-unbranded spread in California against 6¢ elsewhere. Its inquiry is open and it has published no findings (DPMO, Jun 2026).

entries.headline: 7. Exports do not explain the 2026 jump.

lines: Gasoline exports since March averaged 899 thousand b/d, compared with 940 thousand in Dec 2025–Feb 2026 (EIA). Exports are structurally high: 172 thousand b/d of finished gasoline in 2008 vs 778 thousand in 2025. That ties U.S. prices to world prices, but exports did not surge during the war. New York Times Co. v. Sullivan

lines: Deliberately deceiving voters at scale should be treated as a crime against self-government. It is a betrayal of the republic, because free elections assume that citizens can give informed consent. When false claims are pushed, amplified, and left standing long after the record has corrected them, that consent is poisoned.

Hannah Arendt named what is at stake. In The Origins of Totalitarianism (enlarged 2nd ed., 1958; the passage is from “Ideology and Terror,” first published in 1953) she wrote: “The ideal subject of totalitarian rule is not the convinced Nazi or the convinced Communist, but people for whom the distinction between fact and fiction (i.e., the reality of experience) and the distinction between true and false (i.e., the standards of thought) no longer exist.” In “Truth and Politics” (The New Yorker, 1967) she argued that factual truth is the ground political opinion stands on: “Freedom of opinion is a farce unless factual information is guaranteed and the facts themselves are not in dispute.” Factual truth, she wrote, “is always in danger of being maneuvered out of the world not only for a time but, potentially, forever.” In “Lying in Politics” (1971), reflecting on the Pentagon Papers, she found that the policy of lying was “chiefly if not exclusively destined for domestic consumption, for propaganda at home and especially for the purpose of deceiving Congress.” In a 1974 interview with Roger Errera, published in The New York Review of Books in 1978, she warned: “a people that no longer can believe anything cannot make up its mind. It is deprived not only of its capacity to act but also of its capacity to think and to judge.”

Current U.S. law protects much false speech. In United States v. Alvarez (2012) the Supreme Court struck down the Stolen Valor Act, and the plurality wrote that “falsity alone may not suffice to bring the speech outside the First Amendment.” Under New York Times Co. v. Sullivan (1964), a public official suing over a falsehood about official conduct must prove “actual malice”: that the statement was made “with knowledge that it was false or with reckless disregard of whether it was false or not.” This section is not a claim about what the courts already punish. It is an argument about what accountability should become: if a free people cannot tell fact from fiction, they cannot govern themselves.
more: Congress, which writes the rules for itself, has betrayed voters by refusing to police its own members' false statements. Cases in this record were pushed by sitting Representatives, Senators, Speakers, and party leaders in the House and Senate. The Speech or Debate Clause (art. I, § 6) protects legislative acts, but not everything a member does in public. In Gravel v. United States (1972) the Court held that a senator's private publication of the Pentagon Papers “was in no way essential to the deliberations of the Senate” and was not protected. In Hutchinson v. Proxmire (1979) it held that “neither the newsletters nor the press release was ‘essential to the deliberations of the Senate’”; the Clause did not shield them.

Even so, the House rarely uses its own discipline. Its historians list 6 expulsions and 29 censures in its entire history. On June 21, 2023, the House censured Rep. Adam Schiff over Russia-related claims (H. Res. 521), 213–209 with 6 present: every yea was Republican and every nay was Democrat. That is a rarely used tool applied along party lines, not a standing accuracy rule.

entries.headline: TIME and ABC News (Australia) reported that a federal judge “ordered President Donald Trump” to restore CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s White House press access.

record.who: TIME (Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary); ABC News Australia (Rudi Maxwell with wires; headline and summary)
record.began: Sep 24, 2026 (TIME article; ABC News Australia headline and summary)
record.ended: No ending date (live, uncorrected as of Sep 24, 2026)
record.duration: same day (live, uncorrected as of Sep 24, 2026)
record.record:
The order expressly leaves the President out. The substance (the administration was ordered to restore the passes) is accurate; the error is naming Trump as the person ordered. Low severity, but the order's text contradicts it. ABC News (US) reported it correctly (“excluding President Donald Trump”). One case per claim: TIME and ABC News Australia repeat the same error, so they share this row. ABC Australia's story is marked Reuters/ABC; Reuters' own wording was not verified, so Reuters is not named. No correction or fact-check found as of Sep 24, 2026. Claim as published: https://time.com/article/2026/09/24/judge-overturns-trump-white-house-media-ban-temporary-order-appeal/ ; https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-24/us-judge-reverses-donald-trump-media-ban-cnn-politico-ms-now/107192236 Also: https://abcnews.com/US/judge-orders-white-house-restore-press-passes-cnn/story?id=136709442 ; https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74823502/cable-news-network-inc-v-trump/
Primary record: TRO, CNN v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-03287-TJK (D.D.C. Sep 24, 2026), ECF 24 ¶2: “Defendants (except for President Trump) and their agents, representatives, and all persons or entities acting in concert with them shall immediately return, reinstate, and restore the White House ‘hard pass’ press credentials…”

classification.basis: Case names TIME’s Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary.

entries.headline: NPR said Trump “barred the Associated Press from the White House” in 2025 over the Gulf of America dispute, presenting it as a precedent for the 2026 ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.

record.ended: No ending date (live, uncorrected as of Sep 24, 2026)
record.record:
In 2025 the AP was kept out of the press pool, the Oval Office, Air Force One and many East Room events, but it kept its hard passes and general access to the White House press facilities. The 2026 action revoked hard passes and blocked the whole complex, so the comparison makes the 2025 restriction look like the 2026 ban. Rated misleading, not false, because “barred” is accurate for specific events. No correction or fact-check found as of Sep 24, 2026. Claim as published: https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/09/23/major-news-outlets-banned-by-trump-will-have-their-day-in-court
Primary record: AP v. Budowich, No. 1:25-cv-00532-TNM (D.D.C. Apr. 8, 2025), ECF 46 at 9: “The parties agree that no AP employee's hard pass has been revoked”; at 12: “both parties agreed that the AP's hard pass status had been unchanged.”

classification.basis: Case names David Folkenflik’s NPR story.

entries.headline: Harris claimed Trump intends a 'sales tax' tariff plan that economists say would cost typical families about $4,000 a year (as the definitive estimate).

entries.headline: Under Trump's administration, gender-affirming surgeries were available on a medical-necessity basis to people in the federal prison system (implying Trump-era practice matched Harris's position).

entries.headline: Repealing the ACA individual mandate in the GOP tax bill would 'boot' 13 million people from the health insurance rolls.

entries.headline: The GOP health/tax plan would 'knock 13 million people off health care.'

record.method: omits that most of the 13M would leave coverage voluntarily

record.record: PolitiFact found no White House announcement or order for a $5,000 DOGE dividend. A private proposal was not an official payment.

entries.headline: A photo showed Joe Biden in a MAGA hat meeting Trump at the White House on November 13, 2024.

record.record: Trump did visit the White House that day. PolitiFact found this photo was not an authentic picture of the meeting. A detector called it likely AI-generated.

entries.headline: Trump posted on X that he was purchasing TikTok for $2.7 billion.

record.who: A TikTok video, also shared on X and Instagram
record.record: PolitiFact searched Trump's X account and found no such post. The screenshot was fake. The TikTok video had 2.7 million views by January 17, 2025.

entries.headline: Trump approved a law requiring a chip implanted in every foreigner.

record.record: PolitiFact found Trump did not approve that law.

entries.headline: A cut clip showed Trump saying he became president because the 2024 election was rigged.

record.record: The words are his. In the full C-SPAN video he was talking about the 2020 election, which he lost, not about 2024. PolitiFact rated the framed claim false as a confession about 2024.

entries.headline: Trump had died, or had a stroke, over Labor Day 2025.

record.who: TikTok videos and posts on X, including the hashtag trumpisdead
record.record: PolitiFact reported he was alive. One TikTok making the stroke claim had more than 3 million views before it was taken down. The hashtag trumpisdead trended on X.

entries.headline: Donald Trump Jr. said on his Rumble show that the United States should have sent weapons to Russia instead of Ukraine.

record.record: FactCheck.org found the audio does not match the February 25, 2025 Rumble episode. His spokesperson said the audio was AI-generated.
